Just endured a 30 minute debugging session with my mothers account as she wanted to make a nice video for my sisters graduation. This required subscribing for exporting which she was totally onboard with. She tried to subscribe to the standard package and it didn’t offer Apple Pay - this is fine, it then waned to use the card attached to her actual Apple email. 

Unfortunately, she hadn’t updated her cards so it declined. I helped her change her card and then tried again - purchase successful, great! Back to her video, she went to export it and the app told her that she required a paid subscription. She had just paid for one, but still followed the app’s guidance which asked her to pay again and then when trying to pay again it said that she already had a subscription. Well okay then, time to export her video. The app then repeated the same thing and we were locked in a loop where the app could not apply the subscription benefits it supposedly said we already have.

We ended up having to pay for the Pro subscription for it to finally be applied to our account and allow us to download the video. Ridiculously unintuitive user architecture and needs to be fixed.

reviews.title: Unsafe
reviews.text: I need video editing software for my dance teaching job so that I can produce music videos and other content for my students. Reading in on the terms and conditions, the apps broad media licensing and commercial use rights where they can use/modify/distribute any and all content - such as faces, voices, likeness of my students- to train AI models or for marketing, makes this an extremely unsafe app to use. I have researched and deleting the content does not guarantee its removal from CapCut’s servers. For my purposes, this is extremely concerning as child safety and wellbeing, especially online, is becoming more and more important (considering things such as the rise of deepfakes). I would hope that anyone wanting to use this service understands the implications and concerns of its use. I also hope that the creators of this app implement higher safety standards and opt-out options for use of MY data/content. The severe lack of user privacy and consent is astounding and a clear mark of how behind the times this app currently is. DO BETTER!!!

reviews.title: From My Favorite App to My Biggest Disappointment
reviews.text:
I used to love CapCut and happily recommended it to other creators. Unfortunately, it has turned into what feels like a scam.

I originally purchased an annual subscription that was supposed to expire in April. Then I purchased another subscription, but instead of renewing in April, I was charged again in February and paid the full annual price all over again.

What makes this even worse is that I shoot all of my content in 4K. I can import my 4K videos into CapCut, edit them, but I can’t export them back in 4K with the subscription I already paid for. Instead, the app downgrades the quality of my own videos to 1080p unless I pay even more.

So after paying for a yearly subscription, I’m now expected to pay another $100 just to export my own 4K footage in the same quality I uploaded it. I genuinely don’t understand why I should have to spend over $200 a year just to trim videos, remove music, and make basic edits.

As a content creator, I need 4K exports for my work. I paid for this app, yet I still can’t use it for what I need. My refund request has not been resolved, and at this point it feels like I’ve simply thrown my money away.

Sadly, I won’t be using CapCut anymore. It’s incredibly disappointing to see an app I once loved become so aggressively monetized that even preserving the original quality of your own videos requires paying for another, even more expensive subscription.

reviews.title: Used to be amazing
reviews.text:
I’ve been using CapCut for about 4 years now, and it was my go to video editing app. The filters were cute, the effects were fun, there was no watermark, and the overall quality was great. It worked super well, and it was largely free, which is something that is rare with good video editing software.  

So tell me why everything costs money now? All of the transitions, filters, effects and stickers are pro-only. Core features have been stripped away and gatekept from free users. Every time I open the app, more and more of my favourite features are pro-only, which is insane for an app which advertises itself as free. I understand that the developers need money too, but at this point you’d be better off making CapCut a single purchase app, instead of advertising it as free and relegating everything to a pro subscription. You’re just losing the trust of your userbase, and that’s sad for an app which was once so highly acclaimed. I’m disappointed, and probably won’t be using CapCut again.

Subscriptions on a surface level are perfectly fine but a once a free app with very little locked features has now been turned into an especially what is a pay to play. If CapCut is going to lock all the features that made them stand out from other mobile editing apps behind a paywall I would genuinely rather pay $100 flat fee than a subscription. I love using CapCut but the direction it’s chosen to move has made it hard to use without paying for a subscription.

reviews.title: Unethical Business Practices
reviews.text: If it was possible to rate an app ‘no stars,’ I would have selected the option. I have been a Capcut user throughout the months and ‘extract audio’ has never been a ‘pro’ feature. Yesterday, I redownloaded and purchased the standard subscription which at the time included extract audio (which was a free option for me at the time of purchase). I proceeded to create two edits for TikTok with no troubles, having zero to no issues with the extract audio feature and have a screenshot from yesterday to confirm. Opened the app today to continue and it’s now listed as ‘pro’ feature and won’t let me access the edit without paying for a pro subscription. As someone who just purchased the standard subscription, I absolutely cancelled it and I commend you to do the same. From someone who studies Business Administration at University, this to me seems to be an unfair business practice. The features included in the app are not worth the price of a pro subscription if you are thinking about purchasing it and what this business has demonstrated is that even if you secured a pro subscription, there’s a chance they’ll create a ‘premium’ subscription which is higher than the pro for basic features which are available for free on online alternatives. Abhorrent behavior, either make the app a one cost purchase or rethink your practices. Disappointed.
